written.myAnswer: Like parallel forces act in the same direction; unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.
The rectangular components of a vector F at angle θ to the positive x-axis are Fx = F cos θ and Fy = F sin θ.
The line of action of a force is the straight line along which the force acts.

The moment (torque) of a force about a point is the turning effect of the force, equal to force times the perpendicular distance from the point to its line of action. If r is the position vector from the point to where the force acts and θ is the angle between r and F, that perpendicular distance is r sin θ. Therefore τ = F(r sin θ) = rF sin θ.

A body moving in a straight line with constant velocity is in dynamic equilibrium because its resultant force is zero.
The centre of mass is the point at which the whole mass of a body may be considered concentrated. The centre of gravity is the point through which the body's total weight acts.
Stability is increased by lowering the centre of gravity and widening the base of support.

In uniform circular motion, the instantaneous velocity is tangential to the circular path while the centripetal force points radially toward the centre. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so the force is perpendicular to the velocity. It changes the velocity's direction, not its magnitude.
The car experiences more centripetal force on the curve with the smaller radius. For fixed mass and speed, Fc = mv²/r, so the force is inversely proportional to the radius.
When the branch is shaken suddenly, the mango tends to remain at rest because of inertia. The stalk is pulled or disturbed and may break, allowing the mango to fall.

An object is more stable when its centre of gravity is low and its base of support is wide. It topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base. For example, a tall narrow box is less stable than the same box laid on a wider face; widening its base makes it harder to topple.
An accelerated body has a non-zero resultant force, so it cannot be in equilibrium.
The taller box is more likely to topple. The inertial effect during the sudden stop acts through its centre of gravity, which is higher, producing a greater turning moment about the base.

The principle of moments states that for a body in rotational equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a pivot equals the sum of anticlockwise moments. For example, a 2 N force acting 0.3 m from a pivot balances a 3 N force acting 0.2 m from it, since both moments are 0.6 N m.

Suspend the lamina freely from one point and hang a plumb-line from the same point. Draw the vertical line along the plumb-line. Repeat from another suspension point. The intersection of the two lines is the centre of gravity.
For equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero and the resultant torque about any point must be zero.

Lower the centre of gravity and widen the base of support. For example, racing cars are designed to be low and wide, and a balancing toy is made with its centre of gravity low so it tends to return upright.
